Code specifically: terminal-native (no IDE lock-in), strong on long-context
tasks like reading a whole replication package, comfortable with non-web

machine.

For the head-to-head with Cursor, ChatGPT, and Copilot, see

:::

## Outline

- "It works wherever your project lives" — runs in your terminal, no
  separate editor required, no need to move your project into a special
  directory.
- "It reads a lot at once" — long context window matters when you ask it
  to audit a 30-file replication package or revise a 50-page paper.
- "It does not pretend to know what it does not" — relatively conservative
  about admitting when it needs to look at a file before answering.
- "It treats you as the principal" — plan mode, todos, and explicit
  permission prompts before risky actions.
